title: Generalizing Concessive Conditionals: akármilyen / bármilyen ... is legyen ('no matter how / whatever it may be')

sections.title: Universal Concession across Indefinite Scales
sections.content: To state that an outcome, truth, or commitment holds without exception, Hungarian combines indefinite pronouns (bármilyen, akármilyen, akármennyi, bárhogy) with the particle 'is' and a conditional or subjunctive verb form: 'Bármilyen nehezek legyenek is a körülmények, az együttműködés folytatódik' (No matter how difficult the circumstances may be, cooperation continues).

sections.title: Subjunctive vs. Conditional Mood in Generalizing Clauses
sections.content: In formal policy, analytical, and academic prose, subjunctive forms (legyen, merüljön fel, alakuljon) frequently replace everyday conditional forms to denote universal openness to all eventualities: 'Akárhogyan döntsön is a parlament...' (However parliament may decide...).

items.spanish: Bármilyen lassú legyen is a tárgyalási folyamat, a határ menti önkormányzatok megegyeznek.
items.english: No matter how slow the negotiation process may be, border municipalities reach agreement.

items.spanish: Akármilyen politikai viták alakuljanak is ki, a gazdasági kapcsolatok megmaradnak.
items.english: Whatever political debates may develop, economic ties remain.

items.spanish: Bárhogy változzanak is a nemzetközi körülmények, a Duna menti partnerség megkérdőjelezhetetlen.
items.english: However international circumstances may change, the Danubian partnership is unquestionable.

sections.title: B2 Usage Notice
sections.content: Always include the postposed particle 'is' in generalizing concessive structures: '[Bármilyen / Akármilyen + Főnév] ... [Ige] is'. The sentence loses its concessive meaning without 'is'.
